correctness.rationale: For lines (a u_j+tJu_j,kt), orthogonal projection onto (Ju_j,k) yields the asserted point-to-line quadratic with first and second discrete Fourier harmonics. On n>=4 equally spaced samples, first harmonic is orthogonal to the sampled second, so coefficient -2ar vanishes only for r=0 (a>0). On n=3 samples cos2v aliases cos(3theta)cos v+sin(3theta)sin v; the independent first-harmonic coefficients give r cos 3theta=4aB and z=r sin3theta/(4k). Exactly three nonaxial components and the axis result. Averaging the squared distance and substituting gives a²[(4B-1)²+(8B(2B-1)+B/k²)tan²3t], strictly convex at each branch minimum. The axis has one minimum, no maxima; for R>0 the axis contributes 0/1/2 and three curves 0/1/2 each, giving 0,1,2,5,8 values. Independent direct line-projection numerical tests for a=1.3,k=0.8 and n=3,4,5 confirmed the branch equalities and axis normalizations; inspected check.py from actual source. Exact Fourier algebra, not samples, proves the all-parameter claim.

evidence: Everett et al. establish the four-branch topology for generic skew triples and axial cubic-plus-line criterion; Papadopoulou–Suderland–Wang obtain global bounds of four maxima/eight minima and a degree-12 critical procedure. Those results cover broad geometry and possible algorithmic calculation, but neither quoted theorem gives this all-a,k closed four-minimum critical spectrum, exact threshold, or the n>=4 equidistance-axis rigidity.

value.rationale: A natural regularly spaced family of skew tangents has a sharp three-versus-four-site harmonic resonance and a complete exact radius-by-radius number of spheres tangent to every line. The transition at a(3+4k²) and complete four-minimum spectrum are useful model cases for multivariate Voronoi, exact tangency and algebraic geometry; this is more than rephrasing an existing cubic-plus-axis branch count.
